chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
When one of you places his hand on his head or beard while in the state of Ihram, and some hair falls out, he should give charity of a handful of food or a handful of Sowiq.

key_terms.سَوِيقٍ: Sowiq (a traditional food made of roasted flour and fat, often used as charity measure)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for accidentally losing hair while touching the head or beard during Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar details the specific expiation (kaffarah) for a pilgrim in Ihram who accidentally causes hair to fall from their head or beard by touching it. The ruling prescribes giving charity in the form of a handful of food or Sowiq (a flour porridge), reflecting the practical and accessible nature of compensatory acts in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the distinction between intentional and accidental violations of Ihram restrictions, emphasizing ease for the pilgrim.
